original_question: Let G be a right-angled Artin group. Is the stable commutator length scl(g) a rational number for every g ∈ [G, G]? For free groups this is true by Calegari’s Rationality Theorem. (See 18.40 for the definition of scl(g).)
target_in_paper: Problem 21.127 (I. Soroko): rationality of stable commutator length in right-angled Artin groups, using the definition of scl from Problem 18.40.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it asks about right-angled Artin groups, restricts to elements g in the commutator subgroup [G,G], asks whether scl(g) is always rational, and keeps the paper’s contextual remark that this is known for free groups via Calegari’s Rationality Theorem. It also correctly points to 18.40 for the definition of scl.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should spell out the definition of commutator length cl(g): the least number of commutators in G whose product is g.
It should explicitly define stable commutator length by scl(g) = lim_{n→∞} cl(g^n)/n.
The quantifier should be made fully explicit as: for every element g of the commutator subgroup [G,G], one asks whether scl(g) lies in Q.
No extra hypotheses should be added: the paper does not restrict to hyperbolic right-angled Artin groups, finitely generated right-angled Artin groups, or any special subclass.

If one wants the wording to be completely self-contained for readers outside the immediate area, one would also need to define the term 'right-angled Artin group'; the paper itself does not restate that definition at Problem 21.127.
refined_question: Let G be a right-angled Artin group. For each g ∈ [G,G], let cl(g) denote the least number of commutators in G whose product is g, and define the stable commutator length by scl(g) := lim_{n→∞} cl(g^n)/n. Is scl(g) a rational number for every g ∈ [G,G]? (For free groups this is known by Calegari’s Rationality Theorem.)
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 21.127 exactly, not the broader neighboring conjecture in Problem 18.40 about hyperbolic groups. Problem 21.127 states essentially the same question for right-angled Artin groups, while Problem 18.40 supplies the definitions of cl(g) and scl(g) that must be incorporated to make the question stand alone. There is no paper-given equivalent reformulation nearby that should replace the direct wording.
